articles.summary: – Completed treatment of all 90 patients in Part A of the pivotal Phase 2/3 MIRACLE trial evaluating Annamycin in relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) – Comprehensive Part A data readout remains on track for the first quarter of 2027, supporting optimal dose selection and planned initiation of Part B – Annamycin’s differentiated cardiac safety profile further supported by peer-reviewed analysis of 90 patients across five clinical trials, with no evidence of clinical or subclinical cardiotoxicity at first interim analysis – New preclinical findings suggest Annamycin may help turn immunologically “cold” pancreatic tumors “hot,” supporting potential combination treatment approaches HOUSTON, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Moleculin Biotech, Inc., (Nasdaq: MBRX) (“Moleculin” or the “Company”), reported on Friday the financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and highlighted continued progress across its clinical development programs, including completion of treatment in Part A of its pivotal Phase 2/3 MIRACLE trial evaluating Annamycin (also known as naxtarubicin) in relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Moleculin continues to advance its lead clinical program following completion of treatment for all 90 patients in Part A of the MIRACLE trial. articles.title: Moleculin Biotech Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results as Pivotal MIRACLE Trial Advances Toward Key Q1 2027 Data Readout

articles.summary: Inhibition of CD8+ T cells shortens survival in Annamycin-treated mice, demonstrating the immune system is a functional contributor to Annamycin’s antitumor activity, not a bystander Annamycin achieves substantially higher pancreatic tissue exposure than doxorubicin, offering a potential explanation for why topoisomerase II, a validated target in pancreatic cancer, has never been successfully drugged there HOUSTON, Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Moleculin Biotech, Inc. (Nasdaq: MBRX) (“Moleculin” or the “Company”) today announced new preclinical data showing that its lead drug candidate, Annamycin (naxtarubicin), combined with PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade, extended survival in pancreatic cancer models beyond that achieved with either agent alone. The findings will be presented today by Waldemar Priebe, PhD, of The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, in an oral presentation at the 6th Annual Marie Skłodowska-Curie Symposium on Cancer Research and Care organized by Moffitt Cancer Center, being held November 8-11, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. The presentation, titled “Targeting pancreatic cancer with Annamycin and turning immune cold tumor into hot tumor,” is scheduled for November 10th at 2:45 p.m. ET during the symposium’s gastrointestinal and urologic malignancies session. articles.title: Preclinical Data Show Annamycin Makes Pancreatic Cancer Responsive to Checkpoint Inhibitors, Opening a Combination Path with Immunotherapies

articles.summary: Patent strengthens intellectual property protection for preparation of preliposomal Annamycin lyophilizate HOUSTON, Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Moleculin Biotech, Inc. (Nasdaq: MBRX) (“Moleculin” or the “Company”) today announced the grant of an Australian patent covering the preparation of preliposomal Annamycin lyophilizate, strengthening the Company’s intellectual property protection for a key aspect of Annamycin’s formulation technology. Australian Patent No. 2020303572 was granted to Moleculin and The Board of Regents of The University of Texas System. The patent titled, “Preparation of Preliposomal Annamycin Lyophilizate,” addresses the preparation of Annamycin’s formulation. “Securing this patent in Australia represents another step in our efforts to build a strong international intellectual property position around Annamycin,” said Walter Klemp, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Moleculin. “Our formulation technology is an important component of Annamycin’s development, and protecting this technology across international markets supports our broader intellectual property strategy.” Expanding International Protection for Annamycin Formulation Technology The Australian patent is part of Moleculin’s broader global intellectual property portfolio covering complementary technologies associated with Annamycin, the Company’s investigational anthracycline. articles.summary: First interim results from pivotal Phase 2/3 trial highlight encouraging remission rates in patients with relapsed or refractory AML HOUSTON, Nov. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Moleculin Biotech, Inc. (Nasdaq: MBRX) (“Moleculin” or the “Company”) today announced that an abstract highlighting data from its lead drug candidate, Annamycin, has been accepted for presentation at the 2026 American Society of Hematology (ASH) Annual Meeting, taking place December 12-15, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. The abstract, titled “A Pivotal Phase 2/3 Study of Naxtarubicin as Second Line Therapy in Patients with AML,” presents results from the first prespecified interim analysis of the Company’s pivotal MB-108 Phase 2/3 trial evaluating Annamycin in combination with cytarabine (Ara-C) in patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Among the first 45 randomized patients evaluated, complete remission rates were 43% and 36% in the two Annamycin treatment arms, respectively, compared to 12% in the placebo arm. Consistent with findings across Annamycin’s clinical development program to date, no signs, symptoms or echocardiographic findings suggestive of cardiotoxicity were observed through the data cutoff.
